FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated in vinegar, {1_plur} and {2_plur}, threaded onto skewers and grilled over charcoal in the street. Born of what the masters would not eat.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} boiled and cold, drowned under a sauce of fresh {1_adj} and yellow {2_adj} passed through a sieve until it turns silken. A first course, never a main.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} hollowed and blanched three times over to take out most of the fire, stuffed with minced {1_plur}, capped with {2_plur} and put in the oven. Three times, and it still burns.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick soup of {0_adj}, {1_adj} and {2_adj}, into which a whole egg is broken at the last moment. The prawn heads make the stock and are never thrown away.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked in {1_adj} stock and a coriander purée that dyes it deep green, with {2_coll}. The colour disconcerts at first, and is then missed when it is not there.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} rinsed at length — its saponin is bitter — then stewed with {1_plur} until it opens its germs into spirals, with {2_plur} melted through it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in a purée of {1_adj} and fermented {2_plur}, until the sauce turns dark green. It is called dry although it swims: nobody knows why.
